Adrian's DeFi Insights

Last cycle I was early on Solana, farmed Hyperliquid before its airdrop and caught the AI narrative before it went mainstream. I still left a lot of money on the table. Not because of bad analysis but because I had no written plan for what to do once I was right, or wrong. Here’s the framework I use now, a first look at my own plan, and a prompt that walks you through building yours. Take your time, this is the most important process to make it in this bull market. Why a plan matters A trading plan decides more than when you buy. It sets how big a position can get, what makes you add or cut, and when the original idea stops being valid. You need it most when the market does something you didn’t expect. Without one, you make the hardest decisions on a red candle with your phone in one hand on the toilet (nobody has ever sized a position well in that setting). With a trading plan, you set the rules while calm. When a trigger hits, you look up what you already decided. What mine looks like (a preview) My own plan runs to 13 sections. I’m publishing the full version next week. Here’s the skeleton: Leverage is still in there. The difference from last cycle is that it now has written conditions for going up and a hard rule for getting out. The open-items list is the part I’d copy first. Once you write down what you haven’t decided yet, you stop deciding it at the worst possible moment. How to build yours (8 steps) 1. Set your goal and time horizon Answer three questions: What am I trying to achieve? With how much capital? Over what period? “I want to make as much as possible” helps with zero decisions later. This works better: “I want to build capital over several years and can accept a portfolio drawdown of up to X USD.” Your horizon decides which information matters. If you hold for months, a 4-hour candle is noise. If you trade short-term, you need tighter rules and more frequent checks. Then check that goal, timeframe and required return fit together. If the goal only works with high leverage, write that leverage into the plan as a risk. 2. Write down where you actually stand Fill this in before you plan any entry: Watch for hidden correlation.
